record.name: Vera Vuković
record.title: Principal Research Fellow
record.bio: Vera Vuković completed her BSc and MSc in Applied Mathematics at the University of Novi Sad (2004, 2007), followed by a PhD in Computer Science from the same institution (2013), with a dissertation on probabilistic imputation methods for sparse clinical time-series. She joined the BioSense Institute in 2014 and was promoted to Principal Research Fellow in 2021. Her group develops computational pipelines for harmonising heterogeneous electronic health record data across multiple hospital systems, with emphasis on ICD code normalisation via ontology alignment, longitudinal missing-data imputation, and supervised models for readmission risk. She teaches a graduate course on biomedical data engineering at the Faculty of Sciences. The group operates a dedicated HPC cluster and maintains curated de-identified EHR cohorts assembled under data-sharing agreements with clinical partners in Serbia and Croatia.
open_to: joint projects with companies handling clinical or health-adjacent data
contract research on EHR data harmonisation and preprocessing pipelines
industrial PhD supervision for candidates with a clinical data background
consulting on ICD code normalisation and ontology mapping workflows
student internships for MSc students in data science or biomedical informatics
record.industry_experience: Vera Vuković served as a paid scientific advisor to a health technology startup in Novi Sad during 2020–2021, providing guidance on EHR data pipeline design for a patient-flow optimisation product. The engagement did not involve intellectual property transfer.
record.notes: Vera Vuković is available for new collaborations from mid-2025 onward; the HARMON-EHR project concluded in 2023 and READICAST enters its final year in 2025, freeing capacity. She has a strong preference for collaborations that include access to real anonymised clinical data rather than purely synthetic datasets, and she is cautious about commitments that would require her team to own or operate clinical IT infrastructure. Any industry partner should be aware that data use agreements with her clinical partners require institutional sign-off and typically take three to four months to complete.
